Although this is an fMRI study using visual drug cues (videos) and reports subjective cue-reactivity, the full text does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or within-participant drug>control fMRI contrasts. The reported results focus on subjective VAS craving measures; no whole-brain activation results, coordinates, figures, or description of voxelwise group analyses, scanner field strength, or processing software are provided in the manuscript excerpt. Therefore the study does not satisfy the requirement for whole-brain task activation evidence and cannot contribute task-evoked whole-brain data to the meta-analysis.

The study used an alcohol taste-cue paradigm (Alcohol > Water contrast based on taste delivery) rather than a visual image-based cue-reactivity paradigm. The meta-analysis requires cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3), which is not met. Although visual words (“Alcohol”/“Water”) were presented before taste delivery, the primary fMRI contrast and reported effects center on taste receipt, not visual cue reactivity. Additionally, the paper emphasizes ROI (ventral striatum) analyses as primary and does not provide a clearly usable whole-brain visual cue Alcohol>control activation map suitable for inclusion. Therefore it does not meet the key modality requirement for this review.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity using visual stimuli with a within-subject CUE>neutral contrast. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps (corrected results, figures and coordinates) and describes preprocessing/analysis using FSL on a 3T scanner. Participant age and sex are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual cannabis cues in adolescents (drug-related visual stimuli). The analysis includes a within-participant contrast of cannabis>non-cannabis cues and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results using FLAME (FSL) with cluster correction. Participant age and sex, cue type (cannabis), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL/FEAT/FLAME) are reported. Results are presented as whole-brain clusters (cluster-corrected maps and supplementary figures), satisfying the requirement that whole-brain results be clearly described. The study is empirical and not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or between-group-only. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This paper describes development and validation of an image database (MOCD) and behavioral ratings; it does not include any fMRI data, within-participant fMRI contrasts (drug>control), or group-level whole-brain task activation maps. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I3 (functional MRI study), I4 (within-participant drug>control contrast), and I5/I6 (whole-brain task-evoked results). It is a methods/validation resource without original fMRI activation results, so exclusion criterion E6 applies.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cocaine cues with a within-participant cocaine > neutral contrast. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and thresholded in SPM8, with results reported as SPM maps, tables of coordinates, and figures. Relevant participant demographics (n, sex), cue type (cocaine), MRI scanner field strength (Siemens 3.0T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Thus the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This study reports an fMRI cue-reactivity experiment using visual alcohol vs neutral pictorial stimuli in a within-participant, placebo-controlled crossover design in heavy social drinkers. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (Fig.5, Table 1) with family-wise error correction and provides coordinates and regional results. Participant age and sex (male-only) and cue type (alcohol) are reported in the text; methodological details (scanner and preprocessing/statistics) are stated to be described in the Supplementary Information. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for an fMRI visual cue-reactivity task, within-subject contrast (alcohol>neutral), whole-brain results, acceptable reporting format, and reported participant/cue information.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cocaine cues (cocaine pictures vs. neutral pictures) with a within-subject contrast (cocaine > neutral). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (one-sample t-test on cocaine>neutral contrast) with corrected thresholds and provides coordinates (e.g., PAG cluster) and supplementary tables/figures. Relevant methodological details are reported (participant sex distribution and age differences, cue type: cocaine, 3-T scanner field strength, and processing software: SPM8). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (food and household images) assessing natural reward (food) cue reactivity with within-subject contrasts (e.g., Highly Processed Foods > Household Items, Minimally Processed Foods > Household Items). Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses were conducted and reported (SPM12 preprocessing, cluster correction via AFNI 3DClustSim), with results described in the text and figures/tables. Participant age and sex (women, 25–40), cue type (food), MRI field strength (3 T), and processing software (SPM12, AFNI) are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3–I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes whole-brain task activations).

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli (drug and food videos). It reports within-participant contrasts comparing drug vs food cues (DRUG>FOOD), and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded and reported with peak coordinates/ROIs and supplementary materials). Relevant participant details (age, sex distribution), cue types (cocaine, food), MRI scanner field strength (3T Siemens TrioTim), and processing software (SPM12) are explicitly reported. Therefore it meets all listed inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual smoking stimuli and includes within-participant smoking>neutral contrasts and adequate reporting of participant demographics, scanner (3T), and processing software (FSL). However, the paper’s task-based cue-reactivity results are reported using a priori ROIs (insula subregions and ACC) with extracted beta weights and regression analyses; no group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or whole-brain task activation results are described in the provided full text. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only task reporting with no whole-brain task results).

This is a task-based fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual alcohol and neutral beverage pictures, with an explicit within-subject contrast (alcohol>neutral). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (AFNI 3dLME, cluster correction) and results reported in tables/figures. Participant age and sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (AFNI) are all reported. Thus the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This study is an fMRI investigation of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in alcohol-dependent patients and controls. It reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol > neutral cues, performs group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (factorial model and interaction effects) with reported cluster/voxel results, and provides methodological details including participant age/sex (male only), cue type (alcohol), 3T scanner field strength, and processing software (SPM8/SPM12). Hence it meets all required inclusion criteria for cue type, contrast, whole-brain reporting, acceptable presentation of whole-brain results, and methodological details.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used visual marketing clips of alcohol and cannabis as cue stimuli and contrasted drug-related clips versus neutral clips within participants. The paper reports individual-level contrasts (alcohol marketing > neutral; cannabis marketing > neutral) and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain GLMs, cluster-level FWE results, figures and tables). Relevant methodological details are provided: participant age and sex, cue types (alcohol and cannabis), scanner field strength (Siemens 3 T), and processing software (SPM8). Results are reported in text, figures and supporting tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study using visual drug-related film cues in amphetamine-dependent participants. It reports a within-subject contrast (Drug movies > Neutral movies) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results with FWE correction. Methods report SPM12 processing, 3 T scanner field strength, and participant age and sex (male, 20–65). Therefore it satisfies criteria for visual cue-related fMRI, within-participant drug>control contrast, whole-brain task activation reporting, acceptable reporting formats, and required participant/scanner/method details.

Although this is an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli (alcohol pictures) and within-subject contrasts, the reported analyses are ROI-to-ROI task-modulated functional connectivity (gPPI) using a predefined 132-ROI atlas. The paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation map (voxelwise activation contrasts); instead results are limited to ROI-based connectivity findings and seed-based PPI-like analyses. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task activation and falls under exclusion criteria for studies reporting only ROI/seed-based connectivity without whole-brain task maps.

This study reports a task-based fMRI investigation of methamphetamine (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures) and reports a within-participant contrast of Methamphetamine Cue > Control Cue. Results are presented as whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<.05) with coordinates/tables and figures. The manuscript reports participant age/sex, cue type (methamphetamine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking cues (nicotine) with an event-related design and within-subject Smoking > Neutral contrasts. The authors performed voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses using FSL/FLAME and report cluster-corrected whole-brain results for Smoking-Neutral (with tables/figures describing activations). Participant age range and gender matching are reported, cue type (nicotine) is specified, scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio) and processing software (FSL) are given. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without unmasked task effects, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.
